newsitem.title: GERMANY: World War Two fighter plane unearthed near Cologne.
newsitem.headline: World War Two fighter plane unearthed near Cologne.

text.p: Construction workers have unearthed the wreckage of a World War Two-era German fighter plane that probably came down during an aerial battle in 1944, German police said on Thursday.
The plane was discovered on Wednesday in the village of Roesrath-Scharrenbroich outside Cologne by workers digging a canal on the site of a future industrial park, police spokesman Kurt Ruland said.
Workers found the pilot's parachute, an intact leather wallet, German military documents, used ammunition and a German military badge in the wreckage, he said.
"We believe it is a German plane and eyewitnesses say it came down in autumn 1944," Ruland said, adding that experts had not yet ascertained exactly what type of plane it was.
Local resident Alfred Brenner said he remembered watching the plane come down as a schoolboy and that a wooden cross had stood on the site for years afterwards in memory of the dead pilot.

Brenner, who was seven at the time, said he used to come there to pick potatoes during the war. He recalled how he and a friend dived to take cover during a fierce aerial battle between the German Luftwaffe and Allied planes.
"There was an aerial battle and suddenly a plane came down and all hell broke loose," Brenner said, describing how it burst into a ball of flame before hitting the ground.
